findings.title: All app modules still load eagerly at import time
findings.body: Each `import()` call in the object literal runs as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, so all 28 app packages are still loaded at module evaluation. Nothing is deferred, so the stated goal of the PR is not achieved. An import failure in any one app also becomes an unhandled promise rejection, or makes every lookup fail. Wrap each entry in a thunk instead, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call it at the use sites.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a calendar Promise to other callers
findings.body: `calendar` in the returned objects is now `Promise<Calendar | null>`. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it, but other consumers of `getCalendarCredentials` (the tRPC/API routes) still treat `calendar` as an instance. They would call methods on a Promise, or treat the always-truthy Promise as a valid calendar. In addition, the promise is created even when `app.variant !== "calendar"` and is never awaited, so a rejection there is unhandled.

findings.title: forEach(async) pushes to apiDeletes after it has been awaited
findings.body: For recurring bookings, the callback now awaits `getCalendar` before pushing deletions into `apiDeletes`. `forEach` does not wait for async callbacks, so `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs before anything is pushed. Calendar event deletions for recurring bookings are therefore not awaited, and any errors from them become unhandled rejections.

findings.title: Async forEach makes calendar and video deletions fire-and-forget
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` returns promises that nobody awaits. Rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` are unhandled and can crash or log noisily. The same pattern in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts` and `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` makes their surrounding try/catch ineffective. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` instead.
